assertions.api_adaptation: Original #37 source callbacks return Promise.reject(Error) or a never-ready Promise. The true native RecordSink wrapper admits the actual callback factory synchronously and polls its returned future on one bounded owned worker. Rejections use payload-free ObserverRejected rather than a JavaScript Error object; private rejection strings are not part of the native typed API. Native returned failures are actual Err results, never detached failing task substitutes. Synchronous factory panics preserve the original private sink failure test message. Never-ready native futures remain pending after both callbacks and after actual response delivery, with pending timeout disabled. Both are genuinely polled, retain admission until explicit owner.close after inference, then are cancelled/dropped and the worker joined. Raw before/after numeric snapshots and drop witnesses prove pending=2 then pending/charged_bytes=0, cancelled=2 and worker_finished=true. Default finite admission bounds are an explicit native library contract, not a bound on arbitrary allocations or blocking callback polls. The source #37 uses AbortSignal.timeout(1000) around the real fetch/body read. Native replay applies a real 1000 ms client operation deadline; additional worker disposition checks occur after inference and before joined cleanup. No source deadline or failed callback is replaced by an unconditional success.
